chunks: Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār, from al-Ḥasan ibn Mūsā al-Khashshāb, from Ghiyāth ibn Kallūb, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Jaʿfar, from his father, peace be upon them both.
A man cut off something from part of another man's ear, and that was brought before ʿAlī عليه السلام, so he exacted retaliation from him.

Then the other man took what had been cut from his ear and replaced it onto his ear with its blood, and it reattached and healed. So the first man returned to ʿAlī عليه السلام and sought retaliation, so he ordered it, and it was cut a second time, and he ordered that it be buried.
And he عليه السلام said: “Retaliation is only on account of the disfigurement.”

key_terms.أُذُنِ: ear, the bodily organ injured in this case
key_terms.الْقِصَاصُ: legal retaliation in kind for an injury
key_terms.فَالْتَحَمَتْ: it reattached or joined back together

ai.seo_question: Why is qisas carried out in cases of bodily disfigurement such as cutting part of the ear?
ai.summary: This hadith describes a case of qisas in bodily injury before Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام regarding part of an ear that had been cut. The ruling indicates that retaliation in such a case is tied to the harm and disfigurement caused, and that restoring the severed part after qisas did not prevent the reapplication of the ruling.
